name: Dual-Domain Deformation Model
definition: A deformation model that integrates time domain polynomials and frequency domain Fourier series into a unified fitting model to represent the dynamics of 3D Gaussian particles. It assumes only rotation q, radiance c, and position µ change over time, while scaling s and opacity α remain constant.
summary: The Dual-Domain Deformation Model explicitly models 3D Gaussian particle dynamics by combining polynomial and Fourier series fitting, enabling efficient 4D reconstruction without per-frame models or implicit neural fields.
